correctness.rationale: For any finite local ring with residue F2, the one-dimensional left socle criterion for Frobenius is proved via generating additive characters; the two exceptions have 2-dimensional J^3 in the original complete classification. In the other 184 rings, the complete list of 17 associated-graded presentations (common G; four characteristic-four A-D; twelve characteristic-two) was reconstructed in an exact standalone quotient computation; each nontrivial multiplication pairing to the 1-dimensional top layer is perfect. This forces the left and right socles of all deformations to equal their order-two final radical layers. The 19 characteristic-two full presentations were independently checked for socle sizes. This reconstructs every implication under the explicit cited classification premise.

originality.rationale: The complete newly published 186-ring classification does not state Frobenius status, generating characters or socle counts. Its duo split and radical Hilbert vectors do not alone imply the Frobenius classification: the substantive missing proof is perfect top-degree multiplication in every graded model. The older minimal-size paper gives examples, not all classes. Exact claim-level published-finding corpus and published-source searches revealed no equivalent coverage; historical search incompleteness is noted.
residual_risks: An unindexed or older publication may implicitly prove a stronger property of these 186 specific rings, though the 2026 classification itself does not state the present invariant.
The 186-isomorphism-class completeness is inherited from arXiv:2611.19962v1 and has not been independently recomputed; all new algebra calculations use its printed presentations.
The exceptional characteristic-four ring 20 was excluded by the Hilbert vector, without an independent exhaustive characteristic-four socle computation; no exact socle count for it is asserted.

value.rationale: Frobenius duality is a natural structural invariant of finite local noncommutative rings (generating characters and duality for codes). Its exact 184/2 distribution in the full 186-class minimal reversible-nonsymmetric census is not an arbitrary isolated slice. The proof uses a transferable filtered perfect-pairing principle, and explains the two obstructions and unexpected coincidence of duo and Frobenius status in precisely this family; no hypothetical downstream theorem is needed.
